subject: Urgent: Renewal — Request for Credit, Term Reset & SLA Add-on
messages:
From: Sarah Byrne <sarah.byrne@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Upcoming Renewal — concerns on price and SLA

Marissa —

Thanks for the renewal notice. We ran the numbers and with current hospital reimbursement pressure, the proposed 6% increase on top of last year’s committed spend puts us at risk of moving away at renewal. Given our growth with the product in pilot sites, we want to continue, but we need one or more of the following concessions to proceed: a 15% renewal credit, reset of committed terms to a 12‑month term at current unit rates, or a formal 99.9% SLA add‑on with penalty language.

Can your team work this through with Procurement and Legal? We have a hard deadline of 2/18 to finalize. I’ve attached our internal usage report.

—Sarah
VP, Digital Ops | Nimbus Health

Attachment: usage_report_Q4.csv (CSV, 24KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Byrne <sarah.byrne@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming Renewal — concerns on price and SLA

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the timing. I’m looping in Aditya (Sales Ops) for usage/price modeling and Priyom from Legal for early redline review. We value Nimbus as a strategic customer and want to find a path to keep the deployment expanding.

Quick notes:
- I can request a renewal credit; need to know whether that should be applied as an up‑front credit or amortized over the term.
- Term reset to 12 months is doable from a commercial perspective but will need a signoff on minimum commitment language.
- SLA add‑on can be offered but the penalty structure is non‑standard and will require executive approval due to potential exposure.

I’ll produce a consolidated proposal by EOD Tuesday (2/11) and include the commercial options so you can take them to Procurement.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Upcoming Renewal — concerns on price and SLA

Team — I ran the usage figures (attached) and sketched three commercial options we can present to Nimbus: 

Option A (Retention Credit):
- One‑time credit of 12% applied to invoice at renewal.
- Must commit to 12‑month term at current list rates thereafter.
- No SLA change.

Option B (Term Reset + Modest Credit):
- Reset term to 12 months, 8% up‑front credit amortized over first 3 invoices.
- Include a 30‑day performance remediation clause; no monetary SLA penalty.

Option C (SLA Add‑on — Exec Escalation Required):
- Reset to 12 months + 5% credit + optional 99.9% SLA with financial credits for outages.
- SLA with credits exposes Redwood to unknown exposure beyond 3 incidents/year cap — needs Exec approval for approval of clause and cap.

My recommendation for a high‑touch customer like Nimbus is Option B as the default. Option C could close the deal but requires executive signoff on the SLA language and the potential exposure.

Attachments: usage_report_Q4.csv, renewal_pricing_model.xlsx (stub)

—Aditya
Sales Operations
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T09:01:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Upcoming Renewal — need exec signoff for SLA credits

Vivek — forwarding the thread. Nimbus is asking for either a significant credit, a term reset, or a formal SLA add‑on. Aditya’s Option C includes a 99.9% SLA with financial credits; Legal notes exposure. They have a 2/18 deadline. Can you weigh in on what level of SLA credit exposure we can accept and whether we can approve a one‑time 12% retention credit (Option A) without escalating further?

For context: annual committed ARR is $710k, current year realized spend ~$645k. Losing Nimbus would be material for Q1. They are a strategic healthcare reference customer.

—Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Upcoming Renewal — need exec signoff for SLA credits

Marissa / team — thanks for the write up. Quick internal guidance:

- We can approve a one‑time retention credit up to 10% without C‑level signoff provided the credit is capped and applied to the renewal invoice only. That should be documented in the SOW amendment.
- Any SLA that includes financial credits beyond a small, capped credit (we typically cap at <$25k/year for mid‑market deals) requires approval from me + CFO and Legal signoff on exact fault definitions & incident caps.
- Given ARR exposure (~$710k), I’m willing to sign off on a one‑time 12% credit if the customer commits to a 12‑month reset and adds a minimum annual consumption clause (we need to protect against immediate churn). However, 12% is above the delegation limit — I’ll need to escalate to the CFO for explicit signoff on the incremental 2%.

If you want to pursue Option C (SLA credits), loop me into the contract redline and I’ll coordinate with Finance and Legal. Otherwise present Option B with the 8% amortized credit as the near term solution.

—Vivek
VP, Revenue Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Byrne <sarah.byrne@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-14T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Upcoming Renewal — concerns on price and SLA

Sarah — thanks for your patience. We want Nimbus to stay and to deepen the relationship, so here’s what we can offer: 

Final Commercial Proposal (subject to legal redline):
- Term: Reset to a 12‑month renewal at current unit rates.
- Credit: One‑time 10% retention credit applied to the renewal invoice.
- SLA: Offer a 99.9% operational SLA add‑on with a capped financial credit policy (max $20k/year), with incident caps and clear definitions of availability windows.
- Conditions: Execution of a short SOW amendment and minimum annual consumption clause to be included.

We hope this lands in the middle of your asks. Vivian (cc’d) from Ops will send the SLA doc and Priyom will circulate the redline. If Nimbus agrees, we’ll prepare DocuSign for signatures — target close by 2/18.

If you’d like, we can also provide a one‑time additional 2% credit (bringing total to 12%) but that requires explicit approval from our CFO and will add 24–48 hours to the timeline. Let me know if Procurement wants us to pursue that route.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Nimbus_Renewal_Redline_v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB); SLA_Proposal_v1.docx (DOCX, 48KB)
